articles.title: Sosteneo Raises Over $500 Million for Clean Energy Infrastructure Fund
articles.snippet: Sosteneo Raises Over $500 Million for Clean Energy Infrastructure Fund ESG Today
articles.text:
Energy Transition / Private Equity & Venture Capital
Sosteneo Raises Over $500 Million for Clean Energy Infrastructure Fund
Kenny Fisher
October 19, 2026
Generali Investments’ clean energy infrastructure investment unit Sosteneo announced that it has secured over €450 million (USD$504 million) in capital commitments for its second flagship fund, including securing over €150 million in new fund commitments and co-investment capital at the fund’s first external close.
Launched in 2025, the fund focuses on construction-ready clean energy infrastructure across European markets, investing where specialist capability across construction, financing and revenue contracting can support asset resilience and long-term value creation. The fund targets investments in physical infrastructure with long-term, stable and visible cash flows across three areas of the energy system, including enabling integration and flexibility, securing clean energy supply, and supporting the decarbonization of industry.
Sosteneo’s predecessor Clean Energy Infrastructure Fund announced its final close last year, raising over €620 million in capital commitments, alongside €80 million in co-investment capital. According to Sosteneo approximately three-quarters of the first fund’s 39 projects are now fully operational. In the second quarter of 2026, Fund I began distributing income generated by its operating assets to investor, and in the third quarter, the fund signed an agreement to sell an interest in an operating asset, marking its first partial realization.
Sosteneo said that the new fund’s first external close includes a new commitment from the largest external institutional investor in its predecessor Fund I, commitments from new institutional investors, and an increased commitment from Generali Insurance Companies, the cornerstone investor in Sosteneo’s flagship funds.
Umberto Tamburrino, Managing Partner and CEO at Sosteneo, said:
“We are pleased with the continued progress of Fund I, with most projects now fully operational after just three years from inception. The commencement of income distributions and the signing of our first partial realisation represent further steps in the maturation of the portfolio. Fund I continues to progress in line with our expectations, providing a strong foundation as we continue to develop the Sosteneo platform and deploy Fund II.”

articles.snippet:
Perennial Wealth Partners has launched as a full-service wealth management practice within Integrated Partners, with six financial advisors collectively managing more than $500 million in client assets.
The post Perennial Wealth Partners Debuts With Over $500 Million In Client Assets appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Perennial Wealth Partners Debuts With Over $500 Million In Client Assets
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 15, 2026
Perennial Wealth Partners Debuts With Over $500 Million In Client Assets
Perennial Wealth Partners has launched as a full-service wealth management practice within Integrated Partners, with six financial advisors collectively managing more than $500 million in client assets.
The Chicago-based practice is owned by eight founding partners who have worked together for years and formed Perennial to deepen their collaboration while providing comprehensive financial advice to high-net-worth individuals and families.
Perennial’s founding team includes Ben Audley, Senior Advisor and Partner; Sam Awad, Principal Advisor and Partner; Greg Bogdan, Principal Advisor, Partner and Chairman; Kurt Helmich, Portfolio Manager and Partner; Michael Im, Chief Operating Officer and Partner; Mary Beth McLean, Principal Advisor and Partner; Brady Peat, Advisor and Partner; and Carrie Shoener, Senior Advisor and Partner.
Six of the eight partners serve as financial advisors. The broader team brings experience from major financial institutions and is positioning Perennial around an independent advisory model designed to support long-term client relationships.
Integrated Partners will serve as Perennial’s registered investment advisor and provide access to an open-architecture business environment encompassing technology, back-office infrastructure, and its CPA partner program.
Perennial plans to operate as a central point of coordination for clients’ financial lives, working alongside CPAs, estate attorneys, and other professionals. Its services include investment management, financial planning, tax coordination, and estate strategy.
The practice serves high-net-worth individuals and families, business owners, executives, professionals, and retirees, with a particular focus on women seeking an active role in managing their financial lives.
Founded in Chicago in July 2026, Perennial chose its name to reflect the team’s goal of maintaining enduring client relationships across market cycles and different stages of clients’ lives.
KEY QUOTES:
“Perennial’s team brings decades of shared experience, longstanding client relationships and a deep commitment to service. Our relationship as a team is an incredible asset for our clients and we’re thrilled to be moving forward to find new ways to deliver incredible service to them.”
Michael Im, Chief Operating Officer And Partner Of Perennial Wealth Partners
“We chose the name Perennial to reflect our commitment to being a consistent, trusted presence for our clients — not just for a season or market cycle, but for the long term. We want to be there for both good times and tough moments, providing financial education to allow clients to make their own empowered decisions as each chapter of life unfolds.”
Greg Bogdan, Principal Advisor, Partner And Chairman Of Perennial Wealth Partners

articles.title: Ortet Launches With $500 Million Commitment From Thoreau To Build Patient-Centered Health AI Platform
articles.snippet:
Ortet launched as a frontier artificial intelligence lab for health with a $500 million commitment from Thoreau. The company is building a full-stack AI platform spanning compute and data infrastructure, frontier research, model development, and deployment.
The post Ortet Launches With $500 Million Commitment From Thoreau To Build Patient-Centered Health AI Platform appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Ortet Launches With $500 Million Commitment From Thoreau To Build Patient-Centered Health AI Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 12, 2026
Ortet Launches With $500 Million Commitment From Thoreau To Build Patient-Centered Health AI Platform
Ortet launched as a frontier artificial intelligence lab for health with a $500 million commitment from Thoreau. The company is building a full-stack AI platform spanning compute and data infrastructure, frontier research, model development, and deployment.
Ortet’s approach centers on developing a patient-focused foundation model designed to connect the biological, clinical, operational, and financial dimensions of health.
The company said many existing healthcare AI systems are built for narrowly defined tasks and limited datasets, which can limit their ability to learn relationships across a patient’s biology, treatment history, outcomes, and interactions with the broader healthcare system.
Ortet is building a shared intelligence foundation that can improve continuously and adapt across scientific discovery, clinical care, healthcare operations, and financial administration.
The company said knowledge developed in one area could strengthen performance in others through a system designed around the individual patient.
Ortet is led by Co-Founder and CEO Kyunghyun Cho, Ph.D.
Cho co-developed the attention mechanism and Gated Recurrent Unit, technologies that helped establish foundations for modern AI architectures.
He is also the Glen de Vries Professor of Health Statistics at New York University.
Before launching Ortet, Cho spent five years building an AI platform focused on lab-in-the-loop molecular design.
He co-founded Prescient Design and later established Genentech’s frontier research team following Prescient Design’s acquisition.
Ortet’s founding team also includes Co-Founder and Chief AI Officer Keunwoo Choi, Ph.D., who previously developed AI systems at Upstage, Spotify, ByteDance, and Genentech.
Henri Dwyer serves as Co-Founder and Chief Technology Officer and previously built and managed Genentech’s largest GPU cluster after engineering roles at Instagram and Lyft.
Jeff Hammerbacher is Co-Founder and Chairman. He is Founder and CEO of Open Athena and previously served as Principal Investigator at Hammer Lab, Founder and Chief Scientist at Cloudera, and Manager of the Data team at Facebook.
Elman Mansimov, Ph.D., serves as Co-Founder and Chief Science Officer and previously worked on neural text-to-image generation as well as post-training and agentic AI platforms at Amazon Web Services.
Claudia Shi, Ph.D., is a Founding Member of Frontier Research and previously worked on AI research and development at Meta Superintelligence Labs.
The $500 million commitment from Thoreau will support development of Ortet’s compute and data infrastructure, health-focused model training and deployment, and continued investment in research and talent.
Ortet has already secured its initial GPU cluster and is building the technical foundation required to move research into production at scale.
The company expects to work with customers across the health ecosystem from launch, using real-world needs to guide development of its models and products.
Goldman Sachs advised on the transaction.
Ortet is a founding Thoreau investment.
Thoreau is building foundational compute, rules, and research infrastructure across healthcare markets including providers, payers, employers, life sciences, and government.

articles.title: Sabey Data Center Properties Secures Additional Ares Investment, Bringing Total Commitment Above $500 Million
articles.snippet:
Sabey Corporation and National Real Estate Advisors announced that Ares Secondaries funds have expanded their investment in Sabey Data Center Properties, bringing Ares’ total commitment to the data center platform to more than $500 million.
The post Sabey Data Center Properties Secures Additional Ares Investment, Bringing Total Commitment Above $500 Million appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Sabey Data Center Properties Secures Additional Ares Investment, Bringing Total Commitment Above $500 Million
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 8, 2026
Sabey Data Center Properties Secures Additional Ares Investment, Bringing Total Commitment Above $500 Million
Sabey Corporation and National Real Estate Advisors announced that Ares Secondaries funds have expanded their investment in Sabey Data Center Properties, bringing Ares’ total commitment to the data center platform to more than $500 million.
The additional investment follows Ares’ minority equity investment in Sabey Data Center Properties announced in July 2026.
Sabey Data Center Properties is a fully integrated owner, developer, and operator of hyperscale and enterprise data centers across the United States.
The platform currently operates data center campuses totaling approximately 275 megawatts of capacity in major U.S. markets.
Its development and expansion pipeline is expected to increase the platform to approximately 737 megawatts by 2033.
The additional capital will support Sabey Data Center Properties as it expands infrastructure to meet increasing demand associated with cloud computing, artificial intelligence, and other data-intensive applications.
Sabey Data Center Properties has more than four million square feet of mission-critical space and serves customers across the technology, financial services, healthcare, and other industries.
The company specializes in scalable data center infrastructure designed around operational reliability, efficiency, and lower total cost of ownership.
Sabey Data Center Properties operates as a joint venture between Sabey Corporation and National Real Estate Advisors, which manages investments on behalf of institutional clients.
The follow-on Ares investment further aligns the three organizations around the continued expansion of the platform.
Ares Management had more than $671 billion in assets under management as of June 30, 2026, with investment strategies spanning credit, real estate, private equity, infrastructure, and secondary markets.
KEY QUOTES:
“This follow-on investment reflects continued conviction in SDCP’s long-term value proposition and growth trajectory. We remain focused on disciplined growth and delivering the digital infrastructure needed to support the next generation of cloud and AI demand.”
Kevin Verdi, Executive Vice President and Chief Investment Officer at National Real Estate Advisors
“We are pleased to deepen our relationship with Ares as we continue executing on our long-term growth strategy. This additional commitment reflects confidence in the strength of our platform and our ability to develop and operate the mission-critical infrastructure our customers rely on.”
Tim Mirick, President of Sabey Data Center Properties
“We are pleased to expand our investment in SDCP and build on our relationship with the Sabey and National teams as we continue to see significant runway for growth.”
Jamie Sunday, Co-Head of Real Estate Secondaries at Ares

articles.title: Pasadena Quantum Startup Oratomic Raises $475 Million, Reaching $5.4 Billion Valuation
articles.snippet: Pasadena Quantum Startup Oratomic Raises $475 Million, Reaching $5.4 Billion Valuation Pasadena Now
articles.text:
Local quantum computing startup Oratomic has raised $475 million in Series B financing, pushing its valuation to $5.4 billion, according to the law firm that represented the company in the transaction.
The financing, announced Oct. 8, brings Oratomic’s total funding to $775 million since its public launch in March. Wilson Sonsini Goodrich & Rosati disclosed the amount and valuation, while Oratomic separately announced the cumulative funding figure.
The round was co-led by ARCH Venture Partners, Spark Capital, Khosla Ventures, Index Ventures, General Catalyst and Bezos Expeditions, Wilson Sonsini said. Oratomic previously raised $300 million in a Series A round announced in July.
Oratomic said the new investment will support growth of its scientific and engineering staff, laboratory infrastructure and the systems required to build its quantum computers. Its announcement did not specify how many jobs would be created or how much of the funding would be spent in Pasadena.
The company is developing quantum computers using arrays of neutral atoms, which serve as quantum bits, or qubits. Focused laser beams hold and rearrange the atoms, allowing researchers to explore methods of correcting errors that can interrupt quantum calculations.
The Pasadena company has strong ties to the California Institute of Technology. Chief Executive Dolev Bluvstein was a visiting associate in physics at Caltech as of March, according to the university. Other members of the founding research team include Caltech physics professor Manuel Endres, theoretical physicist John Preskill and Hsin-Yuan (Robert) Huang. Caltech said in March that Huang, an assistant professor of theoretical physics, was on leave while serving as Oratomic’s chief technology officer.
In March, Caltech announced that a team of Caltech and Oratomic researchers had proposed a quantum error-correction method that could reduce the number of qubits needed for a useful machine from millions to as few as 10,000 to 20,000.
That finding is theoretical, not evidence that such a computer has been built. Caltech said the approach still faces substantial engineering challenges, including increasing the size of atomic arrays while keeping error rates low.
In its July funding announcement, Oratomic said it intended to focus on building a fault-tolerant quantum computer rather than developing intermediate commercial products. The October financing gives the company additional resources for that effort. Its October announcement did not establish a timetable for completing a working system, although Oratomic said at its March launch that its mission was to build utility-scale quantum computers by the end of the decade.

articles.snippet:
SmartCentres Real Estate Investment Trust has closed $450 million in senior unsecured debenture financing, consisting of an additional $150 million of its Series AC debentures and a new $300 million Series AE issuance.
The post SmartCentres Closes $450 Million Senior Unsecured Debenture Financing appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
SmartCentres Closes $450 Million Senior Unsecured Debenture Financing
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 20, 2026
SmartCentres Closes $450 Million Senior Unsecured Debenture Financing
SmartCentres Real Estate Investment Trust has closed $450 million in senior unsecured debenture financing, consisting of an additional $150 million of its Series AC debentures and a new $300 million Series AE issuance.
The additional Series AC securities carry an annual interest rate of 3.599% and mature on June 12, 2029. The new Series AE debentures carry an annual rate of 4.795% and mature on January 15, 2032.
Combined with $250 million of Series AC debentures previously issued, SmartCentres now has $400 million in aggregate principal amount of Series AC debt outstanding.
The Canadian REIT plans to use the net proceeds from the latest financing to refinance existing debt, repay amounts outstanding under its revolving credit facility, repay mortgages, and support general corporate purposes. 1
The offering was completed through a syndicate led by Scotiabank, CIBC Capital Markets, Desjardins Securities, RBC Capital Markets, and TD Securities as joint bookrunners. National Bank Financial, Mizuho Securities, Beacon Securities, and Casgrain & Company served as co-managers.
Morningstar DBRS assigned the debentures a BBB credit rating with a stable trend.
The financing adds longer-duration unsecured capital to SmartCentres’ balance sheet while giving the company additional flexibility to address existing debt and mortgage obligations.
SmartCentres is one of Canada’s largest fully integrated real estate investment trusts. Its portfolio includes 201 properties across the country spanning value-oriented retail, purpose-built rental housing, office space, and self-storage.
The trust reported approximately $12.1 billion in assets and 35.5 million square feet of leasable space. Its portfolio was 98.1% occupied or committed, with properties located across approximately 3,500 acres of owned land in Canada.
The new financing also supports SmartCentres as it continues development and intensification initiatives across a portfolio that includes major retail properties as well as increasingly diversified mixed-use real estate.

articles.title: Oxide Raises $445M Series D as the Company Proves Vision of Full-Stack Cloud Infrastructure Enterprises Can Own
articles.snippet: Oxide Raises $445M Series D as the Company Proves Vision of Full-Stack Cloud Infrastructure Enterprises Can Own PR Newswire
articles.text:
Oxide Raises $445M Series D as the Company Proves Vision of Full-Stack Cloud Infrastructure Enterprises Can Own
News provided by
Oxide
Oct 09, 2026, 09:00 ET
Share this article
Share this article
Eclipse leads financing as Oxide reaches profitability and AMD Ventures invests in its systems-based approach to enterprise computing
EMERYVILLE, Calif. , Oct. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Oxide Computer Company , the on-premises cloud computing company, today announced it has raised a $445 million Series D led by Eclipse , with participation from existing investors US Innovative Technology Fund (USIT), Riot Ventures, Jane Street, and more. New investors Atreides Management and AMD Ventures also joined the round.
Oxide entered rarefied air earlier this year as it reached profitability, a significant milestone for a rapidly scaling hardware company. With customer demand exceeding current production capacity, the Series D provides additional working capital to secure components, increase manufacturing and serve new and existing customers.
"The accelerating pace of on-prem cloud computing projects has required us to scale manufacturing capacity by 20x over the past 12 months, and yet demand still exceeds supply," said Steve Tuck, co-founder and CEO at Oxide. "We're well-capitalized, and hit an important profitability milestone earlier this year. This funding will allow us to aggressively invest in the materials and manufacturing scale our customers need for years to come."
Oxide's growth comes as the rise of agentic AI intensifies demand for infrastructure that can support a growing mix of compute, memory, networking and data-intensive workloads. The level of complexity required to support these agentic workloads is only achievable or scalable with full-stack systems – something that historically only the world's largest cloud providers could offer and at a price point that is cost-prohibitive for many organizations. With demand for compute, memory and data center capacity outpacing supply, even the hyperscalers are struggling to keep up. These dynamics reinforce that enterprises need the ability to own and control the systems their most critical workloads run on in order to ensure on-demand access to reliable, secure and cost-effective computing.
The Oxide Cloud Computer is a rack-scale integrated system with purpose-built hardware and open-source software that brings the architectural model of the hyperscale cloud to an organization's own data center. By co-designing compute, storage, networking, and software as a single system, Oxide gives enterprises cloud automation and agility with direct ownership over their security, performance, data, and economics.
"The next infrastructure bottleneck is already taking shape. As AI shifts from generating answers to executing work, demand for CPU-based systems is accelerating dramatically," said Seth Winterroth, Eclipse partner. "Oxide was built for this moment. Steve, Bryan, and the team saw years ago that enterprises would need cloud-scale computing they could own and control, and they built the full system to deliver it. Now they're scaling to meet a market that is moving faster than anyone anticipated."

articles.title: Helen Of Troy: Q2 Sales Rise 2.1% As Company Raises Fiscal 2027 Profit Outlook
articles.snippet:
Helen of Troy reported fiscal 2027 second-quarter net sales of $440.9 million, up 2.1% from $431.8 million in the prior-year period.
The post Helen Of Troy: Q2 Sales Rise 2.1% As Company Raises Fiscal 2027 Profit Outlook appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Helen Of Troy: Q2 Sales Rise 2.1% As Company Raises Fiscal 2027 Profit Outlook
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
Helen Of Troy: Q2 Sales Rise 2.1% As Company Raises Fiscal 2027 Profit Outlook
Helen of Troy reported fiscal 2027 second-quarter net sales of $440.9 million, up 2.1% from $431.8 million in the prior-year period.
GAAP net income totaled $4.6 million, or $0.19 per diluted share.
Adjusted income reached $19 million, representing adjusted diluted EPS of $0.79 compared with $0.59 a year earlier.
Gross margin expanded to 52.2% from 44.2%.
Adjusted operating margin increased to 8.6% from 6.2%, while adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 11.2% from 8.4%.
Cash flow from operations reached $57.1 million compared with a $10.5 million use of cash in the prior-year quarter.
Results included $26.9 million of gross pre-tax tariff refunds, approximately $23 million of which Helen of Troy reinvested during the quarter.
The company said the net pre-tax benefit from tariff refunds was approximately $4 million.
Helen of Troy reduced total debt to $672.6 million from $893.2 million a year earlier.
Inventory declined to $480.3 million from $528.9 million.
For fiscal 2027, Helen of Troy narrowed its net sales outlook to between $1.768 billion and $1.822 billion.
The company raised its GAAP diluted EPS outlook to $3.63 to $4.26 and adjusted diluted EPS guidance to $3.60 to $4.15.
Adjusted EBITDA guidance increased to $203 million to $210 million.
Helen of Troy also raised its expected operating cash flow to $163 million to $179 million and free cash flow to $120 million to $140 million.
KEY QUOTES:
“Our second quarter results reflect continued progress against our multi-year roadmap. Sales were in line, and Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EPS were better than expected, without including the net tariff refund benefit in the quarter.”
“While there is still meaningful work ahead, we are encouraged by the progress we are making to build a Better Helen of Troy on the road to becoming a Bigger Helen of Troy.”
G. Scott Uzzell, CEO of Helen of Troy

articles.title: Wingspire Equipment Finance Raises $407.07 Million In Third Equipment Securitization
articles.snippet:
Wingspire Equipment Finance has raised $407.07 million through WEF 2026-1, its third equipment asset-backed securitization and largest ABS transaction to date. The transaction issued six classes of notes.
The post Wingspire Equipment Finance Raises $407.07 Million In Third Equipment Securitization appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Wingspire Equipment Finance Raises $407.07 Million In Third Equipment Securitization
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 5, 2026
Wingspire Equipment Finance Raises $407.07 Million In Third Equipment Securitization
Wingspire Equipment Finance has raised $407.07 million through WEF 2026-1, its third equipment asset-backed securitization and largest ABS transaction to date. The transaction issued six classes of notes.
Senior notes received AAA ratings from Fitch Ratings and Kroll Bond Rating Agency.
Investor demand exceeded the available securities by more than five times, according to Wingspire.
WEF 2026-1 is backed by equipment lease and loan contracts representing an aggregate securitization value of approximately $438.18 million as of the August 31 initial cutoff date.
The portfolio consists of 211 contracts across 63 obligors.
The latest securitization follows Wingspire Equipment Finance’s $201 million inaugural ABS issuance in 2024 and a second transaction that raised more than $292 million in 2025.
The company has increased the size of its ABS issuance in each of its three transactions.
The financing adds capital capacity as Wingspire continues expanding large-ticket equipment financing for middle-market and private equity-backed companies.
Wingspire Equipment Finance funded $701.3 million of volume during 2025, representing a 66% increase from 2024.
Wingspire Equipment Finance is the equipment financing arm of Wingspire Capital, which is a portfolio company of Blue Owl Capital Corporation.
KEY QUOTE:
“Three ABS transactions in three years, each larger than the last, demonstrate the scale and execution Wingspire Equipment Finance brings to the market. Our third ABS transaction gives us greater capacity to deliver on large opportunities and continue growing alongside the businesses we serve.”
Eric Freeman, Chief Executive Officer of Wingspire Equipment Finance
